{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"645113ac279d121b4d25e7a977904479d2b1a98f2e6f956394744d575621e276","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:15","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle Registration, Ownership Documents and Title","heading":"C2 — KG hints for Vehicle Registration, Ownership Documents and Title","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — KG hints for Vehicle Registration, Ownership Documents and Title

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
The title is held by the legal owner or lien holder, while the registration certificate is issued to the purchaser and must be kept in the vehicle [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint ownership-documents; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F04 and sec04-F05.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A02
A registration address change is a written notice within thirty days, while a registration name change requires appearing in person within thirty days with the endorsed title [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint registration-changes; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F09 and sec04-F10.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A03
Cars carry plates front and rear, while motorcycles, trailers, semi-trailers and mopeds carry a plate on the rear only [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint plates; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec04-F24 and sec04-F25.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A03
A temporary permit runs until the out-of-state registration expires but never beyond twelve months, while a Hawaii registration expires at the end of its own twelfth month every year [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint registration-periods; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F21 and sec04-F05.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A02
A new vehicle from another state needs a manufacturer's certificate of origin or a notarized bill of sale, while a used vehicle from another state needs the title, the registration and a notarized bill of sale from the named seller [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint ownership-documents; prereq_hint sec04-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F16 and sec04-F19.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A03
A used vehicle from a title state needs one notarized bill of sale, while one from a non-title state needs two, covering both the current and the previous sale [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint ownership-documents; prereq_hint sec04-R05; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F19 and sec04-F20.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A01
Cars, buses and trucks show proof of motor vehicle insurance at inspection, while motorcycles show proof of liability coverage [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint registration-requirements; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec04-F02 and sec04-F01.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A02
A stationed service member resident elsewhere may keep an out-of-state registration and skip the Hawaii taxes and fees, while a fully disabled veteran is exempt only from registration fees [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint exemptions; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F11 and sec04-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A01
Mail renewal must reach the county within ten working days before the end of the expiration month, while the registration itself expires at the end of that month [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint registration-periods; prereq_hint sec04-R04; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F07 and sec04-F05.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A02
A new foreign-bought vehicle needs a dealer bill of sale, a compliance label and a seventeen-character identification number, while a used foreign-bought vehicle needs a registration certificate and a bill of sale [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint ownership-documents; prereq_hint sec04-R05; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec04-F17 and sec04-F18.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0022]
